findings.title: The Industrialization of "ClickFix": Inside ErrTraffic
findings.summary_md: Hudson Rock's original disclosure of ErrTraffic, a ClickFix delivery suite promoted by the actor LenAI on Russian-language forums and sold for $800. The tool injects a single script tag into compromised websites, renders fake glitch, font, or CAPTCHA lures, fingerprints the victim OS, and copies a PowerShell command to the clipboard. A campaign dashboard in the report showed a 58.8 percent conversion rate (20 downloads from 34 views), with Lumma, Vidar, and Atomic (AMOS) among the deliverable stealers.

findings.title: Unveiling ErrTraffic: inside a growing ClickFix malware distribution framework
findings.summary_md: Sekoia's TDR team published detailed research on the ErrTraffic ClickFix framework, which had grown from Hudson Rock's late-2025 disclosure into subscription malware-as-a-service with rentals rising from $300 to $380 per month in the first half of 2026. The report documents two operator clusters, Analytics and Beer, that inject the framework into compromised WordPress sites, resolve C2 through EtherHiding smart contracts on the Polygon blockchain, and deliver Vidar, Stealc, Remus, Salat, and SmokeLoader. It also publishes a detection pattern for ErrTraffic's XOR-decoding PowerShell commands based on ScriptBlockText logging.

findings.title: Apple adds macOS Terminal warning to block ClickFix attacks
findings.summary_md: Apple introduced a security feature in macOS Tahoe 26.4 that blocks pasting and executing potentially harmful commands in Terminal and alerts users to the risk. BleepingComputer framed it as a direct platform-level countermeasure to ClickFix attacks on macOS users.

findings.title: Australia warns of ClickFix attacks pushing Vidar Stealer malware
findings.summary_md: The Australian Cyber Security Center (ACSC) warned organizations about an ongoing malware campaign using the ClickFix social engineering technique to distribute the Vidar Stealer info-stealing malware. BleepingComputer's coverage is an early government-level warning on the technique.

findings.title: Ghost CMS SQL injection flaw exploited in large-scale ClickFix campaign
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported a large-scale campaign exploiting a critical SQL injection vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-26980 in Ghost CMS to inject malicious JavaScript that triggers ClickFix attack flows on compromised publications.

findings.title: Hackers hijack thousands of sites for ClickFix and FakeUpdate attacks
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported on DriveSurge, a threat actor operating large-scale malware distribution campaigns using ClickFix and FakeUpdates techniques on thousands of compromised websites.

findings.title: Opera rolls out Paste Protect feature to fight ClickFix attacks
findings.summary_md: Opera introduced Paste Protect, a browser security feature designed to block ClickFix-style attacks that trick users into executing malicious commands pasted from web pages. BleepingComputer described it as one of the first browser-side mitigations aimed specifically at paste-and-run social engineering.

findings.title: Microsoft warns of TerminalFix attacks deploying reverse tunnels
findings.summary_md: Microsoft warned about TerminalFix, a ClickFix variant that uses fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA prompts on compromised websites to trick victims into running malicious PowerShell commands in Windows Terminal and then deploys reverse tunnels. BleepingComputer reported the warning nine days before this story's first_seen.

findings.title: Over 5,400 hacked sites serve ClickFix payloads stored on the blockchain
findings.summary_md: BleepingComputer reported a massive cybercriminal operation leveraging more than 5,400 compromised small-business websites to deliver ClickFix payloads stored in smart contracts on the BNB Smart Chain. The article was published four days before this story's first_seen and shows the WordPress ClickFix injection ecosystem operating at scale.
